Title: The Effect Of Thinking About Being Excluded By God On Well-Being: A Replication And Extension
Author: Anna R. George
Abstract: Diverse samples and replication are two important aspects of scientific research. Our research replicates a previous study, which examined how Christians being led to believe God will either include or exclude them influenced well-being scores.
decisions.reason: Parent read the two complete available abstracts: Davidsson/Honig2003venturecreation human/socialcapital named in current title/abstract matches618; rareGod-inclusion/exclusion wellbeingmanipulation and specificthesis replication/meta-analysis match2385vanBeest/Williams, not a new paperfromblankidentityfields. The SMART single-blind trial explicitly interrogates earlier verbal/intellectual gains under strongercontrols, with actualcomparisons to Cassidy2011pilot verbalIQ, Hayes/Stewart2016verbal/blockdesign/activecomputercontrol findings, Amd/Rochedosageeffect inBangladesh andThirus2016controlledRavenintelligence claim. Current IQ/MatrixReasoning and training-level analyses are actualtests, not onlyinterventionreuse. Printed references and documented differing designs/samples distinguishpublishedreports from20Cassidy2016; no assertion of every participant disjoint across uninspected originalbodies. All outcomesremainunknown rather than transferredfromgenerictraininggain. This decision resolves this specific described/named original identity, without promoting the blind coding or transferring an outcome.

decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state file exists for this work. The primary source is an abstract-only thesis record stating that it replicates a single previous study ('Our research replicates a previous study, which examined how Christians being led to believe God will either include or exclude them influenced well-being scores' and 'A mini meta-analysis was conducted on our data and the original authors’ data, which showed a large effect of thinking about God’s abandonment on well-being'). The thesis title ('The Effect Of Thinking About Being Excluded By God On Well-Being: A Replication And Extension') and experimental paradigm directly match shipped row input_row_index 2385 (van Beest & Williams, 2010, '“Why Hast Thou Forsaken Me?” The Effect of Thinking About Being Ostracized by God on Well-Being and Prosocial Behavior', DOI 10.1177/1948550610393312, verified in Crossref metadata). Blind target 0 left bibliographic fields blank only because the abstract-only source lacks a reference list, and it is already represented by shipped row input_row_index 2385.
